sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for web reading
sections.what: Loads the web request, HTML reading, table and logging tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: these cover downloading, reading and tabling data.

sections.name: fetch_url
sections.title: Downloading a page
sections.what: Downloads a page and returns its text, or nothing if anything goes wrong.
sections.why: Likely reason: returning nothing instead of crashing lets research continue past one bad page.
sections.watch_out: A caller that does not check for nothing will fail later with an unclear error.

sections.name: parse_html_tables
sections.title: Reading tables from HTML
sections.what: Reads every table in an HTML text into a list of tables, or an empty list if reading fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared way to turn web tables into data the code can use.
sections.watch_out: A page with no tables and a failed read both return an empty list, so they look the same.

sections.name: extract_text
sections.title: Pulling text with a CSS selector
sections.what: Finds the first element matching a CSS selector and returns its text with spaces trimmed, or nothing if there is no match or an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a scraper pick one value, such as a title or a number, from a page.
sections.watch_out: A selector that matches the wrong element returns text from the wrong place with no warning.

summary: Provides three small helpers: download a web page, read every table on a page, and pull the text from one element chosen by a CSS selector.
purpose: Shared web reading tools for research code.
why: Likely reason: keeps the download and reading steps in one place so other scrapers can reuse them.
how: 1. Download: requests the page with a timeout, checks for an error code, and returns the text or nothing. 2. Tables: reads every table in the HTML into table objects, or returns an empty list on failure. 3. Text: finds the first element matching a CSS selector and returns its trimmed text, or nothing.
inputs: A web address and a timeout in seconds (default 30). HTML text. A CSS selector text.
outputs: Page text or nothing. A list of tables. A text value or nothing.
risks: Every error is logged and turned into an empty result, so a caller may treat a failed download as no data. The download sends no identifying browser header, so some sites may refuse it. There are no rate limits or retries. Table reading needs the lxml library.
debug: If a fetch returns nothing, read the error line in the log for that address and try it in a browser. If tables come back empty, check that the page has HTML tables and that lxml is installed. If text is missing, test the CSS selector in the browser's developer tools.
